precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers.
precepts.point: They intended evil and imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” That sounds just like Malachi 4: “the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”, and “it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Nuclear fire is coming to America. And David goes on: “Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Neither root nor branch: their children will be cut off too.

Isaiah shows why the children are cut off: “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers.” For the sins of their forefathers. The forefathers committed the crime, got the bag from us, took the wealth, took everything from us, and now the children are left holding the bag. Esau, and not just Esau: Elam, Ishmael, the Hamites. All of them got wealthy off the backs of the Israelites; all of them had us in slavery one way or another.

It is done “that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” Son and nephew goes right back to Psalm 21 and the end of Malachi 4: their seed destroyed from among the children of men.

Why? “For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” They imagine evil devices and evil counsels against us, but “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword.” The poor are Israel: “the poor of his people shall trust in it.” So the fiery oven is for the nations that enslaved us, down to their children, and the Lord saves his poor from their sword.

precepts.text: For behold the day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly shall be stubble; this is the day of the Lord.
precepts.point: Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger; the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath and the fire shall devour them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” Malachi tells when: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.”

This is the day of the Lord. The day comes that burns as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly are stubble, burned up so that neither root nor branch is left. That is the fiery oven of the Most High's anger, the fire that devours them.

precepts.text: The Lord sends his sword, fire, and plagues, and none can turn them back.
precepts.point: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth and their seed from among the children of men; Esau is not going to be no more. They imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform; the Most High makes their devices of none effect and makes ready his arrows against the face of them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
“Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Esau is not going to be no more. Ezra shows there is no stopping it: “A sword is sent upon you, and who may turn it back? A fire is sent among you, and who may quench it? Plagues are sent unto you, and what is he that may drive them away?”

“May any man drive away an hungry lion in the wood? or may any one quench the fire in stubble, when it hath begun to burn?” The Lord sends his sword, fire, and plagues, and none can turn them back. They imagined a mischievous device they are not able to perform, but the Most High's arrows are made ready against the face of them, and nobody drives them away.

precepts.text: This shall be the plague: their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, their eyes in their holes and their tongues in their mouth; that is a nuclear bomb. We saw it at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the weapons have only got more advanced; the Most High is manipulating that weapon so the earth turns into a microwave.
precepts.point: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth and their seed from among the children of men; Esau is not going to be no more. They imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform; the Most High makes their devices of none effect and makes ready his arrows against the face of them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
The arrows the Most High makes ready against the face of them: “And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.”

Flesh consuming away while they stand on their feet, eyes in their holes, tongues in their mouth: that is a nuclear bomb. We saw it at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the weapons have only got more advanced. The Most High is manipulating that weapon so the earth turns into a microwave.

That is how their fruit is destroyed from the earth and their seed from among the children of men. They imagined a mischievous device, but the Most High makes their devices of none effect and turns his own plague on all that fought against Jerusalem.
